object_description: solitary row building along the street divided into two structures by a passage
design_condition: the long building uses the perimeter optimally along the traffic route, standing on a plateau at the street and opening the space towards the neighbouring school complex, with the gymnasium lowered to give the school wing cubic prominence

positive: The available space is optimally used along the traffic route
The resulting open space offers an opening towards the neighbouring school complex
The two- to three-storey vertical development makes a clear statement about the intended use
Parking is arranged in a spacious underground garage with a covered bicycle shelter
The plateau along the street highlights the main entrance and creates a seating and resting area
Access to the garage and bicycle shelter is correctly provided via the existing access road
The connection to the existing school complex is directly guaranteed by bicycle and pedestrian paths
The longitudinal building is divided into two structures with a passageway as break hall
Lowering the gymnasium creates a cubic effect corresponding to the importance of the school wing
The spatial relationships are clearly defined and designated by four entrances
The different school types are clearly arranged and the layout is symmetrical
The open spaces serve the flexible use of the structures
The west-east orientation of the school use is correct
Multi-storey atriums light the interior spaces naturally
Day and evening operation is possible without any problems
Access areas and stairwells are clearly arranged for problem-free school operations
Multifunctional rooms generate added value, the auditorium can be enlarged and the two-storey library is viewed positively
The solid construction has a clear vertical and horizontal load-bearing structure
The canopy of the sports hall is continued on the school wing so the building appears uniform
The main entrance is clearly marked by the entrance gallery
Facade panels and floor-to-ceiling windows complement each other in a uniform grid facade
The lightness of construction and facade corresponds to the flanking buildings and leads to acceptance
negative: The structure only moderately zones the outdoor space due to the large building area
The relocated access could also have been located to the south
The naturally lit interiors appear modest in places
The classrooms lit from one side are naturally poorly lit at the rear given their 8.20 m depth
An intercepting ceiling is required above the underground parking garage
Tension piles are needed at the gymnasium floor slab to prevent uplift
